messages:
alex: Heads up — we've started seeing gRPC streaming stalls hitting production after the HAProxy roll yesterday. Affected endpoints are the user-stream fanout (1->N) paths. First noticed around 09:02 UTC.
monica: Saw this too, e2e chats getting truncated or resumed with big gaps (200-800ms). Not consistent per-user, looks correlated with requests that fan out to 3+ backends.
raj: Any errors in the proxies? HAProxy logs look clean but I see lots of `http2 stream reset` on the backend side.
dave: I pulled a tcpdump from the edge during an incident window. Pattern: client->edge h2 frames keep coming, then a burst of RST_STREAMs to backends, followed by a pause, then client keeps sending. Looks like backend connections are being torn but client is not retried. Snip: `RST_STREAM code=0x2` mixed with `WINDOW_UPDATE` spikes.
alex: Pasting small haproxy stat line we correlate: `queue=0, cur_sess=12, srv_conn=36, srv_queue=0, maxconn=200`. Nothing obviously maxed but there was a short spike of `maxconn` on one backend pod.
monica: Could be connection reuse + http2 multiplexing off vs on mismatch. We recently flipped `option http-use-htx` on the edge to prepare for buffering improvements.
raj: Also saw NAT translations on the egress nodes cycling quickly — ephemeral port churn high for the fanout flows. Could be translation TTL and backend half-close interplay.
dave: Repro steps I'm using: 1) open 1 gRPC client stream -> server fans out to 4 workers -> each worker streams partial updates -> therapist: intermittent pause 300-700ms on ~1/30 streams.
alex: Quick check: HAProxy config currently has `timeout http-keep-alive 30s`, `timeout tunnel 2m`, and `option http-buffer-request` enabled. Any recent OS kernel tweaks on egress nodes?
raj: We applied ephemeral port reuse (tcp_tw_recycle-like tune) last week for NAT density, might be relevant. Rolling that back for one host now.
monica: Also noticed that trailers are getting stripped for some streams — backend emits `grpc-status` in trailers but client never receives it when stall happens. Could be trailer handling bug in HAProxy h2 implementation.
dave: Temporary mitigation: adding server-side retry/fallback in the fanout aggregator to detect stalled fanouts and re-request missing chunks. But that's app-level and messy.
alex: Can someone grep kernel configs on the egress pool? `sysctl -a | egrep 'tw_reuse|tcp_tw'` should show what changed.
raj: Confirmed: `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1` and `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` narrowed to 32768-60999 to save ports. We can widen range and disable aggressive reuse.
monica: I opened an HAProxy issue about trailers + h2 half-close interaction — there's a note in their changelog about intermittent trailer drops when `http-buffer-request` is on. Linking: https://github.com/haproxy/haproxy/issues/xxxx :eyes:
sre-bot: Incident alert created: IN-2026-1885 — streaming-edge-stall. Owners: @eng-infra, @eng-runtime.
dave: Doing a quick A/B: disable `http-buffer-request`, widen port range to 10240-65535 on one node, and flip off tcp_tw_reuse. Rolling those changes to a canary host.
alex: ETA for canary?
dave: 5-10m. I'll watch logs and client telemetry.
monica: If the canary looks good, we should revert the HAProxy htx option cluster-wide and revert sysctl on egress nodes, then run a controlled roll.
raj: Also adding metrics for `h2 stream resets`, per-backend `srv_conn` spikes, and ephemeral port exhaustion.
alex: Action items: dave (canary + telemetry) ; raj (metrics + sysctl rollback playbook) ; monica (bug report + config diff review). If canary passes, plan a 30-min maintenance window. :thumbsup:
monica: FYI when this hits dev env I can reproduce reliably with a local haproxy instance and a 4-worker fanout script, happy to share the test harness.
dave: Canary is up — first 15 minutes look clean, no RST burst, trailers delivered normally. Rolling to 4 more egress hosts.
alex: Nice. Keep monitoring for 2 hours. If anything flares, revert. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
